pages: To whoever digs this out of the rubble. My name does not matter, they will have taken it off the door by now. I was the one who rang the bell.

They came the way the sickness came, slow, and nobody ran, because nobody knew it was an attack. A tall one in a dark cloak walked up our street at night, and the golems let him. Then the men behind him started on the doors.

I rang until the rope burned through. I thought it would bring the golems. It brought my neighbours out of their houses instead, into the street, into the light, and that was what the men had waited for. I rang them out to die.
If any of us are still standing in the ash when you come, and they will be, ring it again. Ring it for them. It is the only thing I know that they still hear.
